correctness.rationale: The 49 equations are uniquely generated by a<=b, a+b<=14. Normalizing c(1)=0 removes a free factor of three. One verifier exhaustively tests all 3^13 normalized colorings with direct bitmask equations, the second uses independent sequential recursion with mathematically safe pruning only after a second violation; both exactly agree with every one of 49 CSV multiplicities, zero defect-free states, 1350 normalized one-defect states and 29 essential equations. A third verifier proves by finite enumeration the 13-integer coloring rigidity underlying the seven-new-equation impossibility, and a direct two-pairs-per-class argument explains that structure. The claim is strictly finite.

value.rationale: Single-equation deletion robustness is a natural invariant of the first minimally unsatisfiable three-color additive Ramsey instance, directly useful for distinguishing equation importance in Schur-number certificates and testing constraint-propagation heuristics. The nonobvious sharp contrast--all seven newly introduced endpoint equations individually redundant although the endpoint causes unsatisfiability--has a rigid-class mathematical explanation, while the exact 29 essential positions and 49-entry multiplicity spectrum measure the core geometry not implied by the classical threshold or 13-integer solution count. This is a complete motivated finite sensitivity classification, not a handpicked slice or just a recomputation of the Schur number.
